t: Savarkar defined a Hindu as one who regards India, from the Indus to the seas, as both fatherland and holy land, and distinguished Hindutva, a national and cultural identity, from Hinduism as a religion.

From the RSS, founded in 1925 after Hedgewar met Savarkar, grew the Sangh Parivar, including the Vishva Hindu Parishad (1964) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (1980), which adopted Hindutva as its ideology in 1989.

Its nature is disputed: some scholars call it fascist or near-fascist, others an extreme conservatism or ethnic nationalism, while the BJP calls it cultural nationalism and not a religious or theocratic concept.
dyk: Savarkar, an atheist, opposed the caste system: under him the Hindu Mahasabha held all-caste dinners in Nagpur and Kanpur, and he gave parents money so that their children of the so-called lower castes would attend school.
ev: Chandranath Basu uses the word in his Bengali book Hindutva: Hindur Prakrita Itihas
Vinayak Damodar Savarkar sets out the ideology in Essentials of Hindutva
K. B. Hedgewar, inspired by Savarkar, founds the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh
The Vishva Hindu Parishad is founded to protect and promote the Hindu religion
The Bharatiya Janata Party is founded
The BJP officially adopts Hindutva as its ideology in the Palampur resolution
The Modi government revokes the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370
Narendra Modi performs the ground-breaking ceremony for the Ram Mandir at Ayodhya

f.thinkers: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, who gave the word its political meaning; K. B. Hedgewar, founder of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in 1925; M. S. Golwalkar, his successor at its head; Syama Prasad Mukherjee, founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh; Balasaheb Deoras, third head of the RSS; Mohan Bhagwat, its head as of 2026
f.texts: Chandranath Basu, Hindutva: Hindur Prakrita Itihas (1892), an early use of the word; V. D. Savarkar, Essentials of Hindutva (1923; later retitled Hindutva: Who Is a Hindu?); Savarkar, “Abolition of Caste” (1930) and The Spirit of Hindutva (1935); the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Palampur resolution (1989)
f.ideas: a Hindu is one who regards India, from the Indus to the seas, as both fatherland and holy land; common nation (rashtra), race (jati) and culture (sanskriti) as the essentials of Hindu identity; Hindutva as distinct from Hinduism the religion; the Hindu nation, Hindu Rashtra; an undivided India, Akhand Bharat; a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens
f.today: the guiding ideology of the RSS and the Sangh Parivar, among them the Vishva Hindu Parishad and the Bajrang Dal; adopted by the Bharatiya Janata Party in 1989 and pursued in part by Narendra Modi’s governments since 2014; also espoused by the Hindu Mahasabha and the Shiv Sena; networks of groups in the United States, the United Kingdom and elsewhere
